Hi all — I validated the usage CSV against our billing ledger. Summary: a provisioning SKU (PROV-PM-01) was auto-applied to accounts that exceeded their onboarding resource allocation during the Aug 15–Sep 2 migration window. That SKU should have been suppressed for Clearwell as part of the onboarding commitment; we missed the suppression flag in the migration job.

Proposed remedy: layered approach
1) Immediate goodwill credit: full removal of the one-time provisioning line (gross €14,850) as a customer courtesy.
2) Metering reclassification: reclassify the provisioning units to standard metered usage and issue a corrected invoice for audit (net change €0, but moves charges into the correct buckets).
3) VAT handling for EU: treat the credit as a correction to the original taxable base. For reverse-charge customers we will issue a credit memo with an annotation and provide our VAT TIN + reverse-charge instruction.
4) Payment routing: we can either apply the goodwill as a credit memo against Invoice 2048 (preferred for your AP workflow) or process a partial refund to the original payment method if you need cash returned.

I’ve attached a draft calculation (calculation-layered-credit.xlsx) and a draft credit memo (credit-memo-2048-draft.pdf).

Questions for Clearwell: preferred path (credit memo vs refund), and whether you need a signed DocuSign acceptance of the credit memo for your records.

If agreed I will: issue final credit memo, push a corrected invoice to your billing inbox, and provide VAT evidence (Redwood VAT TIN: GB987654321).

Thanks — Monica
